THIS CRIMINAL PETITION IS FILED UNDER SECTION 482 OF  CR.P.C. SEEKING TO QUASH THE IMPUGNED COGNIZANCE ORDER  DATED 27/03/2023 AND ALL FURTHER PROCEEDINGS IN Sri Raju S/O. Suresh Baddi vs Sri Ramesh S/O. Balusa Baddi on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112419477/
1  C.C.NO.3339/2023 FOR THE OFFENCES PUNISHABLE UNDER  SECTIONS 420, 504 AND 506 R/W SECTION 34 OF IPC ON THE FILE  OF JMFC-I COURT HUBBALLI, INSOFAR AS PETITIONER/ACCUSED  NO.1 IS CONCERNED.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE  COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:7979  CRL.P No. 103130 of 2023  ORDER
Though this petition is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel appearing for both the parties, the same is heard and taken up for final disposal.

2. The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., to quash the impugned cognizance order dated 27.03.2023 and further proceedings in C.C.No.3339/2023 for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 504 and 506 read with section 34 of IPC.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as they are referred to in the Trial Court.
4. The petitioner is accused No.1 and respondent is the complainant before the Trial Court.

5. The summary of the case of the complainant is that, respondent/complainant has filed a private complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C. against the petitioner alleging that the complainant and the petitioner started cloth store in the name and style of 'Balakrishna Kids' at Marata Galli, Hubballi,
by availing loan from Gokulam Finance, Bajaj Finance, KVG Bank and other financial institutions and till 2019 it was running smoothly without any obstacles.

On 03.10.2018, the NC:
2024:KHC-D:7979 petitioner along with accused No.2 conspired against the complainant to close all the existing loan accounts, which were jointly held in the name of petitioner and de-facto complainant in various financial institutions and then made the complainant to believe that they should clear all debts and to open a single loan account in Hubli Urban Co-Operative Bank, Hubballi by mortgaging the property documents pertaining to the complainant.

The petitioner and another conspired together and made the complainant to pay outstanding loan of Rs.80,00,000/- and thereafter the complainant in order to clear outstanding dues, sold his land and paid loan amount.
In fact, the petitioner, accused No.2 and the complainant together agreed to clear the loan amount borrowed by Hubballi Urban Co-Operative Bank.
But they have cheated the complainant by avoiding their liability to clear off the loan dues.

Hence, the complainant approached the petitioner and accused No.2 to clear off loan amount to be payable to the Bank, as such, the petitioner and accused No.2 informed that, it is for him to clear the loan amount, since his land was mortgaged to the Bank and hence, they took quarrel with complainant, abused him in filthy language,
intentionally insulted and made criminal NC: 2024:KHC-D:7979 intimidation to eliminate him.
Thus, the complainant filed the private complaint.

sentences.text: Soon after initiation of the complaint, the Trial Court took cognizance and recorded the sworn statement of complainant as PW.1 and marked in all 46 documents and issued process against petitioner and accused No.2.
Taking exception to the same, accused No.1 filed this petition to quash the entire proceedings.
7. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the impugned order of taking cognizance and entire criminal proceedings are baseless.

The complainant was running a cloth business in his individual capacity and the petitioner is no way concerned with the business and financial transactions of the complainant, as per Annexures-C & D, which are rent agreement and GST certificate, showing the name of complainant alone
, thus, the complainant was sole proprietor of Balakrishna Kids Cloth Store.
Since, complainant suffered huge loss in his business, he is trying to blockmail the petitioner to make good his loss by filing false case.
Further the ingredients of Sections 420, 504 and 506 read with Section 34 of IPC would not be attracted.

It is contended that,
the private complaint filed by the complainant is not supported by affidavit NC: 2024:KHC-D:7979 and the cognizance taken by the Trial Court is also not in accordance with law and the Trial Court has taken the cognizance in a mechanical manner.
Hence, the counsel prayed to allow the petition.
8. Learned counsel relied upon the following decisions.

i. Priyanka Srivastava and Another Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Others1 ii. Mallikarjuna and others Vs. The State of Karnataka, through theh police Inspector, Hosapete Town Police Station and another2 iii.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for complainant contended that there is prima facie case against petitioner.
Further, to substantiate the contention of the complainant, he himself examined as PW.1 and 46 documents have been placed on record.
Hence, there is sufficient material to frame charge against petitioner and another.

Thus, he prayed to dismiss the petition.
10.

In view of the submission made by the learned counsel for petitioner and respondent, the following points that would arise for Court consideration as follows:
(2015) 6 SCC 287 ILR 2018 KAR 354 (2023) 3 SCC 423 NC: 2024:KHC-D:7979 "Whether the petitioner made out sufficient grounds to quash the proceedings under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., as sought for?"

11. It is the case of the de-facto complainant that, the petitioner and another committed cheating,
intentionally insulted him and made criminal intimidation, hence, he lodged the private complaint.

12. Perused the entire order sheet of the Trial Court in PCR.No.72/2023 (C.C.No.3339/2023),
wherein the Trial Court recorded the sworn statement/examination of complainant on 23.06.2023 and relied upon in all 46 documents and on 19.09.2023, the Trial Court proceeded against the accused persons for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 504 and 506 read with Section 34 of IPC.
Cognizance literally means knowledge or notice, and taking cognizance of offence means taking notice, or becoming aware of the alleged commission of an offence.
In this case, the Trial Court has taken cognizance of offence before he could proceed to trial.

sentences.text:
At this juncture learned counsel for the petitioner contended that in view of the ratio laid down in the case of Priyanka Srivastava's case (supra), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court held that, if the private complaint filed by the NC: 2024:KHC-D:7979 complainant is not supported by an affidavit,
the private complaint cannot be maintainable.

14. A careful reading of Priyanka Srivastava's case (supra) more particularly paragraph Nos.29, 30 and 31, it clearly establishes that, a private complaint was lodged and matter was referred under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C., for investigation.

Therefore, whenever the matter referred to Police under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C., which necessarily would proceed by Sections 154(1) and 154(3) of Cr.P.C.,
there must be an affidavit accompanying the complaint.

The said affidavit would be a supportive to the complaint, so that the person making the application under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C., should be conscious and also endeavor to see that no false affidavit is made.
In that context, once an affidavit is found to be false, he will be liable for prosecution in accordance with law.

Hence, in that context,
the Hon'ble Apex Court made it clear that, once an investigation is order under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C., the Court must be satisfied that, affidavit of the complainant has been filed or not and the Trial Court be ascertained through an affidavit.

Whereas in this case, the complainant filed private complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C., and the magistrate himself inquired the matter and not referred the case under NC: 2024:KHC-D:7979 Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. and, thus said ratio is not applicable to the case on hand.

15. Insofar as the application of offences under Sections 420, 504 and 506 of IPC, from the perusal of the complaint and other materials on record, prima facie it reveals that the complainant made out the allegations so as to attract aforesaid sections.
In this case, the petitioner has disputed the question of fact that cannot be gone into under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., and hence, it requires a full-fledged trial.
In the instant case, the petitioner-accused No.1 has taken contention that a false case has been registered by the complainant making allegation that, the petitioner and another cheated him.

Whether the petitioner involved in the matter or not, whether complainant alone was running shop, and he alone borrowed loan, since he suffered loss he blackmailing accused is a matter of trial, it requires evidence and it is purely question of fact.
16. Further, disputed question of fact cannot be adjudicated upon by this Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., at this stage, only prima facie case has to be seen.

The similar NC: 2024:KHC-D:7979 issue was laid down in the case of Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt.Ltd. Vs. State of Maharashtra and others4.
17.

entities.text: Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt.Ltd. Vs. State of Maharashtra and others4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, from perusal of the complaint, prima face discloses cognizable offence in the complaint and hence, once cognizable offences are found in the allegations made in the complaint, it is not just and proper to quash the entire proceedings.
Hence, there is no merit in the contention of the petitioner.
18. Accordingly, the petition is dismissed.
19. In view of the dismissal of the petition, pending applications, if any, do not survive for consideration and accordingly the same are disposed off.
